title: Disprove a claim with a counterexample

sections.skill: Find a counterexample that disproves a general mathematical claim

questions.prompt: A counterexample to a claim about every case is one case where the claim is false. Claim: for every whole number n, n squared + n + 11 is prime. Which n is a counterexample?
A counterexample to a claim about every case is one case where the claim is false. Claim: for all numbers a and b, if a > b, then a squared > b squared. Give a counterexample.
questions.correct_answer: any values that satisfy: a > b and a^2 <= b^2 (example: a = 1, b = -2)

questions.prompt: A counterexample to a claim about every case is one case where the claim is false. The claim "every odd number greater than 1 is prime" is disproved by the number 9.

A counterexample to a claim about every case is one case where the claim is false. Claim: 2 to the power n, plus 1, is prime for every whole number n from 1 to 6. What is the smallest n that disproves it?
A counterexample to a claim about every case is one case where the claim is false. Claim: every multiple of 4 is a multiple of 8. Which number is NOT a counterexample?

sections.relationship: Students cannot hunt for a counterexample until they know that one failing case disproves a "for every" claim, and that examples that work prove nothing.
sections.author_note: Students cannot hunt for a counterexample until they know that one failing case disproves a "for every" claim, and that examples that work prove nothing.

questions.prompt: What is a counterexample to the claim "every number with property P has property Q"?

choices.text: A number with property Q that does not have property P
A number with property P that does not have property Q

questions.correct_answer: A number with property P that does not have property Q

questions.prompt: One counterexample is enough to show that a claim about every case is false.
If a claim works for five examples, it is proved true for every case.
A counterexample to a claim about every case is one case where the claim is false. Which number is a counterexample to "all prime numbers are odd"?
A counterexample to a claim about every case is one case where the claim is false. Claim: every whole number divisible by 3 is divisible by 6. Give a counterexample from 1 to 30.
questions.rule: isInteger(n) and n >= 1 and n <= 30 and mod(n, 3) == 0 and mod(n, 6) != 0
questions.correct_answer: any values that satisfy: isInteger(n) and n >= 1 and n <= 30 and mod(n, 3) == 0 and mod(n, 6) != 0 (example: n = 9)

questions.prompt: A counterexample to a claim about every case is one case where the claim is false. Claim: (a + b) squared = a squared + b squared for all numbers a and b. Give whole numbers a and b that disprove it.
questions.correct_answer: any values that satisfy: (a + b)^2 != a^2 + b^2 (example: a = 1, b = 1)

questions.prompt: A counterexample to a claim about every case is one case where the claim is false. Claim: the square root of (a + b) equals the square root of a plus the square root of b, for all numbers a and b that are 0 or more. Which pair is a counterexample?

A counterexample to a claim about every case is one case where the claim is false. Claim: n factorial plus 1 is prime for every positive whole number n. (n factorial is 1 x 2 x ... x n.) What is the smallest n that disproves it?
A counterexample to a claim about every case is one case where the claim is false. The claim "if n squared is a multiple of 4, then n is a multiple of 4" is disproved by n = 2.
A counterexample to a claim about every case is one case where the claim is false. Claim: every rectangle with perimeter 20 has area 25. Which rectangle is a counterexample?

sections.relationship: Expert: claims that hold for many cases before failing.
sections.label: EXPERT CHALLENGE

questions.prompt: A counterexample to a claim about every case is one case where the claim is false. Claim: for whole numbers a, b and c, if a divides b x c, then a divides b or a divides c. Give a counterexample with a, b and c each from 2 to 12.
questions.rule: isInteger(a) and isInteger(b) and isInteger(c) and a >= 2 and a <= 12 and b >= 2 and b <= 12 and c >= 2 and c <= 12 and mod(b * c, a) == 0 and mod(b, a) != 0 and mod(c, a) != 0
questions.correct_answer: any values that satisfy: isInteger(a) and isInteger(b) and isInteger(c) and a >= 2 and a <= 12 and b >= 2 and b <= 12 and c >= 2 and c <= 12 and mod(b * c, a) == 0 and mod(b, a) != 0 and mod(c, a) != 0 (example: a = 4, b = 2, c = 6)

questions.prompt: A counterexample to a claim about every case is one case where the claim is false. Claim: 2 to the power n, minus 1, is prime whenever n is prime. The smallest counterexample is n = 11.
Which claim is FALSE?

choices.text: The sum of two even numbers is even.
If n squared is odd, then n is odd.
If n is prime, then n + 2 is prime.
If n is odd, then n squared is odd.

questions.correct_answer: If n is prime, then n + 2 is prime.

questions.prompt: A counterexample to a claim about every case is one case where the claim is false. Claim: every whole number from 1 to 30 is a sum of two square numbers (0, 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, ...; a square may be used twice). What is the smallest counterexample?

A counterexample to a claim about every case is one case where the claim is false. Claim: for every positive whole number n, 2 to the power n is greater than n. Why is n = -1 NOT a valid counterexample?

choices.text: The claim is only about positive whole numbers, and -1 is not one.
Because a counterexample must be a large number.
Because 2 to the power -1 is greater than -1.

questions.correct_answer: The claim is only about positive whole numbers, and -1 is not one.
